name: Acute Bronchitis
description: An acute inflammation of the large airways, usually caused by a respiratory virus, producing cough with or without mucus. Uncomplicated acute bronchitis generally resolves without antibiotic treatment.
physical_examination: Assessment of temperature, heart rate and respiratory rate
Evaluation for focal findings suggesting pneumonia
recommended_investigations: Chest X-ray only when pneumonia or another serious diagnosis is suspected
Pulse oximetry when shortness of breath or respiratory compromise is present
Influenza or SARS-CoV-2 testing when epidemiologically and clinically indicated
red_flags: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Abnormal vital signs or focal lung findings suggesting pneumonia
Symptoms lasting more than approximately 3 weeks or recurrent episodes
contraindications: Routine antibiotics are not recommended for uncomplicated acute bronchitis.
Do not use coloured sputum alone as evidence of bacterial infection.
